messages:
Sam: Heads up — since yesterday's NF4/FP4 handoff rollout we're seeing ~20-35% throughput drops on 512/1024-seq requests and occasional host memory spikes. Not universal, affects a subset of hosts in ash-region.
Alex: Can you paste the perf numbers and any kernel-selection traces you have?
Sam: Quick summary: production QPS steady but tail latency up, p50 similar. Example: model-x nf4 fp4 canary: throughput down 28% at seq=512, MEM spike +1.2GB transient, CPU overhead up ~12%.
Sam: Profiling snippet from the kernel selection trace (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T21:10:12Z] kernel_selector: chosen=quant4_systolic_v2 score=0.42 latency_est=3.4ms
[2026-03-17T21:10:12Z] kernel_selector: candidate=quant4_fastpath score=0.37 latency_est=2.1ms fallback_cost=1.8
[2026-03-17T21:10:12Z] kernel_executor: executing=quant4_systolic_v2 path=slowpath
[2026-03-17T21:10:12Z] kv_cache: eviction_batch=512 used=82% headroom=18%
```
Maria: Interesting — selector picked a "systolic_v2" kernel that we normally avoid at small batches. Looks like scoring changed after the calibration tweaks. Also KV eviction percentage is high; could be thrash when batches spike.
Lee: Did the autoscaler or batching config change with the rollout? We had a heuristic tweak to prefer kernel with lower mem after last week's PR, but I thought that targeted cold-start.
Orin: (from commit log) we landed perf/selector: prefer_quant_vs_latency weight tweak (hash abc123) + prefetch backoff adjust. That was meant to prefer faster low-latency kernels but maybe interacts badly with mixed-precision profiling.
perf-bot: telemetry alert: "kernel_throughput_regression" xhosts: {ash-2a-*, ash-2b-*} models: model-x, model-y. p90 latency +40% on quant4 canary. See https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/4521
Alex: Can you run a kernel-selection debug on one of the problematic hosts with KG=2 and batch=256/512 distribution? Also include allocator snapshots.
Sam: Running now, attaching a fuller trace (excerpt):
```
-- host ash-2a-07 --
batch_dist: 1-64: 48%, 65-128: 28%, 129-512: 18%, >512: 6%
kernel_scores: quant4_fastpath=0.32, quant4_v2=0.41, quant4_compat=0.27
alloc: total=48GB used=41.2GB slab_frag=6.3% kv_cache_live=3.1M keys
host_event: prefetch_miss spike @21:10:11 count=312 latency=1.8ms
```
Maria: The distribution shows more mid-range batches than usual (129-512 bump). That can push the selector into choosing a kernel with different memory/latency tradeoffs. Also kv_cache_live looks big — possible fragmented eviction leading to memcpy bursts.
Lee: Could calibration have changed the microbench numbers used by the selector? If calibration promoted quant4_v2 by updating its net_latency_est it would explain why choice moved.
Orin: Yes, calibration pipeline updated the model profile yesterday (calib run #20260317-09). It altered per-seq latency for quant4_v2 down by ~10% in microbench—likely noisy because we had a small sample for long sequences.
Sam: Reproduced locally in canary: when forcing selector to score based on older profile, throughput returns to baseline. So this is probably a calibration drift that caused the selector to prefer a kernel that underperforms for our real workload distribution.
Alex: Short term mitigation options?
Maria: 1) Rollback the profile update for the affected models (fast). 2) Force-select the legacy kernel for batches >=128 via an override rule. 3) Increase KV cache headroom to avoid eviction/memcpy thrash.
Lee: I can open a hotfix PR to add guard rails in the selector: if batch_percentile(75) > 128 and kv_headroom < 25% then bias away from systolic_v2. Cheap and quick.
Orin: Also recommend a calibration sanity check: require n>=30 samples for seq>=512 before overriding profiles. We'll add that to the calib pipeline.
Sam: Applied a canary override (force legacy for model-x on ash-2a hosts) — initial numbers: throughput +18% recovered, mem spike gone on that host.
perf-bot: telemetry note: alert muted for host group ash-2a after policy changes.
Alex: Good. Who owns the follow-ups? We need: 1) revert or re-run calibration with higher sample size, 2) selector guard PR, 3) KV cache diagnostics + slowpath backoff.
Orin: I'll take calib pipeline changes (issue #789). Lee will own selector guard PR (PR #4321). Maria owns KV diagnostics and a small allocator fix. Sam will run canary sweep and attach perf dashboards.
Maria: For KV diagnostics I'll add a higher-res metric for eviction latency and memcopy bursts, and run one-off heapdump on a repro host tomorrow.
Sam: Noted — I'll keep the canary pinned to legacy kernel for 24h and post results. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Lee: Long-term: we should include workload-aware validation in calibration — run the calib profile against a small real-traffic sample to catch these distribution skews.
Sam: Agreed. Putting task list into #eng-runtime-issues/789 and will update in an hour.
Orin: Closing loop — we should also add a post-rollout retention window that keeps old profiles for N days for easy rollback.
Sam: Will do.
